Variegated

/VAIR-ee-uh-gay-tid/ - the stress falls on VAIR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Variegated means marked with patches of different colors; diversified.

The koi pond's celebrity is a variegated carp, its back a drifting map of orange, white, and ink black.

Worked Example

The weaver's prize yarn is variegated, dyed so that a single strand slides from teal through copper to cream every arm's length. Knitted up, no two rows of the scarf repeat, and buyers at her stall keep turning the finished pieces over, hunting for a pattern that was never there.

Variegated is more exact than 'colorful' because it describes how the color sits: in distinct patches or zones of different colors across one surface — a leaf edged in cream, a hillside quilted by autumn. Colorful only promises brightness; variegated promises a map. Gardeners use it almost technically, for leaves carrying two or more colors at once.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

mottled: blotched irregularly, usually in two muddled shades

dappled: spotted with soft patches of light and shade

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

plain: one unbroken color throughout

monochrome: confined to a single color

Where it sits · how many colors break the surface — two-tone → speckled → variegated

two-tone vs. variegated: Two-tone allows exactly two colors in orderly blocks, well short of variegated.

speckled vs. variegated: Speckled goes further than two-tone, scattering flecks of another color about, but it stops short of variegated, whose surface breaks into whole patches of several colors.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vari

Root — vari: varied, spotted (Latin varius)

Root — eg

Root — eg: to make, drive (Latin agere)

Suffix — -ated

Suffix — -ated: made, marked

Put it together

Put it together: Vari (varied) + eg (to make) + -ated = made varied. Latin variegare was the craftsman's verb for working different colors into one surface — mosaic floors, dyed cloth. English kept the workshop sense: a variegated leaf or yarn looks deliberately worked, patch against patch, as if someone had made the variety by hand.

Use the root in a new word: variance

Use the root in a new word: variance: The auditor flagged a variance between the warehouse count and the ledger.

Word Choice

descriptive / technical

Variegated is the precision tool of gardeners, geologists, and catalog writers: it says the colors sit in distinct patches on one surface. Mottled blurs the patches into blotches; dappled scatters soft spots of light. Figuratively it can mean diversified — a variegated career — but in this unit protean owns change over time; variegated is variety you can see all at once.
